items.title: Google DeepMind loses ground in elite AI talent as rivals step up hiring
items.summary: Rivals have meanwhile strengthened their ability to attract departing DeepMind employees. Of researc
items.content:
Rivals have meanwhile strengthened their ability to attract departing DeepMind employees. Of researchers and advanced engineers who left DeepMind over the past year, 25 per cent moved to Anthropic, 21 per cent joined Meta and 14 per cent went to OpenAI, according to Zeki.

The corresponding arrivals-to-departures ratios were around 22-to-1 for Anthropic, 5.7-to-1 for OpenAI and 3-to-1 for Meta in the periods covered by Zeki’s analysis.

The numbers coincide with a series of high-profile departures from DeepMind.

Jeff Dean, the company’s long-serving chief scientist, left after 27 years and joined Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le in launching AI startup Discovery Loop. [...] Other prominent researchers, including David Silver, Wojciech Czarnecki and Lasse Espeholt, have also left DeepMind. Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou departed in 2024 to establish Reflection AI.

The movement has extended to some of DeepMind’s best-known AI projects.

In June, Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer left DeepMind for OpenAI, following Google’s reported $2.7 billion deal to bring him back from Character.AI. John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Demis Hassabis for work on AlphaFold, also moved to Anthropic.

Several AlphaFold researchers, including Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel, subsequently followed Jumper.

items.title: Threat Actors Abuse Cursor Agent AI to Assist Ransomware Operations - Infosecurity Magazine
items.summary: On other occasions, specific instructions were given relating to which exploitation tool to use or t
items.content:
On other occasions, specific instructions were given relating to which exploitation tool to use or to follow a previously generated attack plan. This included enumerating the domain to report which privileges a supplied user holds, using NetExec’s BloodHound collector and scanning the internal subnets for hosts with Nmap or NetExec.

Cursor Agent was also tasked with various exploitation activities, such as attempting NTLM relay attacks by coercing authentication with PetitPotam, Coerce Plus, and PrinterBug and running certificate attacks with Certipy.

The agent was also told to instal a VPN client or proxychains, then configure it and connect to a victim with supplied credentials or an existing SOCKS tunnel. [...] While Cursor Agent did not always achieve its stated objectives, the research demonstrated how threat actors are continuously experimenting with AI tools to speed up and enhance their campaigns.

Cursor Agent is used by software developers to complete complex coding tasks independently, run terminal commands and edit code.

## How Aurora Abuses Cursor Agent in Ransomware Attacks

The Aurora operators deployed Cursor Agent to assist with post-compromise activities, providing the tool with credentials or an existing route into the victim organization.

Some of the commands given to the agent related to providing intelligence on the victim’s environment. In some cases, the attacker only asked Cursor Agent to achieve a stated objective, such as “tell me what rights the user has.” [...] Infosecurity Magazine Home » News » Threat Actors Abuse Cursor Agent AI to Assist Ransomware Operations

items.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI - TechCrunch
items.summary: On Friday, Anthropic published a new paper titled “Automated Researchers Can Reliably Mitigate Align
items.content:
On Friday, Anthropic published a new paper titled “Automated Researchers Can Reliably Mitigate Alignment Failures,” detailing how AI systems could reliably improve a model’s performance on a set of alignment benchmarks. When given 10 benchmarks for specific misaligned behaviors, the automated systems were able to improve performance on every single one without degrading overall performance. [...] Led by Anthropic Fellow Chen Yueh-Han, the system replicates much of the traditional approach to research. Each automated system searches the available literature, proposes a method, and trains the model using that method for 30 minutes, gradually increasing the benchmark over several iterations. Effective methods are preserved while ineffective ones are discarded, allowing the system to operate quickly and at a great scale.

“Overall, these results provide early evidence that automated alignment post-training could become practical in the near term,” the paper reads. [...] The paper is a step toward recursive self-improvement, which many see as the next significant step in AI progress. If models can improve their own alignment training, it’s plausible they could improve training practices more broadly — at which point, human AI researchers might soon become obsolete.

The paper isn’t shy about addressing this idea, explicitly comparing the Automated Alignment Researcher (AAR) to its human equivalent. “The best AAR method beats what experienced humans propose, on average within six hours,” the paper reads. “Human guided research directions do not lead to stronger performance.”

There’s even a cost comparison, in case anyone wasn’t convinced. “An AAR costs roughly $4 per hour in API inference against the $150 per hour we pay our human researchers.”

items.title: Why 95% of AI Pilots Fail — and What Imran Tariq and Jun Xiong Do Instead - Time Magazine
items.summary:
Stop Asking AI Questions. Start Giving It a Job.

Tariq and Jun Xiong co-founded Prime Movers AI on
items.content:
Stop Asking AI Questions. Start Giving It a Job.

Tariq and Jun Xiong co-founded Prime Movers AI on the same premise the MIT data ended up confirming: most companies aren't failing at AI because the models are weak. They're failing because they're asking a search engine to do a workforce's job. "You don't win deals with clever prompts," Tariq has said. "You win by recognizing patterns and responding with precision." A chatbot that only responds to prompts can still be useful, but its role may be closer to an information-retrieval tool than an active part of a company’s workflow.

The Trouble Begins When Growth Depends on One Person's Memory [...] Tariq's own answer to why so many AI initiatives stall traces back further than Prime Movers AI. He co-authored The Pyramid of Trust with Aimee Tariq, Lisa Fei, and Tyler Wagner, a book about what has to be true before people act on what they're told. MIT's data is the same argument in numbers: a tool nobody trusts to touch the real workflow never gets the chance to prove itself, and 95% of the time, it doesn't get one. That instinct, built over many years when he was running Webmetrix Group and recognized in many media appearances, as well as contributing to TechCrunch, is what shaped the four-system model Tariq and Xiong built together. [...] The report's lead author, Aditya Challapally, named the pattern behind the number: "Almost everywhere we went, enterprises were trying to build their own tool." Homegrown AI succeeds roughly a third of the time. Tools developed with outside expertise and tailored to a company’s specific workflows may be more effective than generic solutions. Tools that cannot adapt to existing workflows may still answer questions effectively but have a more limited impact on broader operations.

其他科研人员表示，考虑到大语言模型已经得到广泛应用，该研究测出的高使用率有合理性。加拿大多伦多大学的Kyle Siler认为，结果说明大语言模型已是“大势所趋、覆水难收”。但他们同时提醒，这项研究的数据未必能够代表全部科学文献，还需要更多分析才能全面掌握整体使用情况。  该研究还发现，相较于方法、结果部分，摘要、引言、讨论部分出现大语言模型使用痕迹的情况更多见。2025年12月的论文样本中，78%的讨论部分检出AI痕迹，而结果部分为58%。  Kobak提出，结果部分由AI辅助完成这一点值得警惕，因为大语言模型有编造数据，也就是产生“幻觉”的倾向。与此同时，用大语言模型撰写、修改引言，有可能扭曲一个领域的主流学术观点。“大语言模型自带的任何偏见都会渗透到整个学术文献体系中。”  英国伦敦大学学院的Andrew Gray指出，目前AI检测工具存在一大缺陷，即无法区分文本是完全由AI生成，还是仅用AI进行了语法润色。“这就导致期刊很难筛选出低质量的AI生成内容，因为无论AI实际参与写作的比重多少，所有经过AI处理的论文都会呈现相似文本特征。”  该研究发现，作者所在国家不以英语为主要通用语言的论文，大语言模型使用更为普遍。Kobak说：“这并不出人意料。非英语母语研究者常会借助大模型翻译文本、打磨语法。”Siler则提出，未来的研究不能只关注谁在用大语言模型，更要聚焦人们究竟如何使用这些工具。  为区分合理使用AI与AI生成劣质论文，许多期刊现在要求作者在投稿时说明AI的使用方式与使用场景。论文第一作者、德国图宾根大学的Lena Holzwarth提醒科研人员，使用这类工具仍需保持谨慎。“反复推敲思考，再把想法落实成文字，是科研过程不可或缺的一环。完全依赖大语言模型写论文，就舍弃了这一关键的思考打磨过程。”  相关论文信息： [...] 其他科研人员表示，考虑到大语言模型已经得到广泛应用，该研究测出的高使用率有合理性。加拿大多伦多大学的Kyle Siler认为，结果说明大语言模型已是“大势所趋、覆水难收”。但他们同时提醒，这项研究的数据未必能够代表全部科学文献，还需要更多分析才能全面掌握整体使用情况。

items.summary:
## Summary

The debate continues over whether AI will democratize technology or concentrate power am
items.content:
## Summary

The debate continues over whether AI will democratize technology or concentrate power among tech giants. While powerful algorithms are controlled by a few corporations, the cost of AI has plummeted, making it significantly more accessible. Small businesses are now adopting AI at an unprecedented rate, often outpacing larger firms in everyday applications like marketing and natural language processing. However, reports also indicate a notable gap in overall AI usage between large and small enterprises, with bigger companies leading in more complex deployments. Ultimately, the future hinges on factors beyond sheer compute power, including regulatory frameworks, human ingenuity, and innovative applications that address real-world needs, suggesting the AI race is still wide open. [...] We often hear that AI will act to “democratize” access to many aspects of technology, from data analytics to coding. But what exactly does this mean?

The basic premise is that by lowering the barriers to entry, activities that previously required large budgets and teams of technical specialists are accessible to any business. Or that’s the theory, at least.

On the other hand, the most powerful algorithms and foundation models are owned and controlled by a handful of giant, multinational corporations. Meaning the advantages they give could be withdrawn at any point, should Google, Amazon or whoever decide to flick the switch, or raise the prices so they become out of reach of smaller companies. [...] Often the barrier preventing smaller businesses from getting involved is a lack of AI literacy and understanding of what the technology offers. As the SBA research shows, many simply don’t believe that AI is applicable, or understand the benefits.

At the end of the day, I don’t believe it will be access to technology or sheer scale of compute power that will really differentiate between winners and losers in the AI race.

Facebook Twitter Pinterest Whatsapp [...] ## Security and Infrastructure in Focus

Several sessions will address the security and infrastructure challenges of AI. Ric Smith, President of Product & Technology at Okta, will lead a technical discussion on why agentic AI requires rebuilding cybersecurity from the infrastructure level, arguing that application-level permission models are fundamentally flawed. Arsalan Tavakoli of Databricks will break down what enterprise AI security requires in 2026, including observability, governance, and architecture. A separate panel with AWS’s Chet Kapoor, Katie Moussouris of Luta Security, and Wendy Nather of 1Password will examine how AI is complicating cloud security.
